title: British Literature — Faith in the English Tradition
description: Test your understanding of British literature from the Anglo-Saxon period to the modern era.

questions.question: In Beowulf, the monster Grendel is described as a descendant of which Biblical figure?
questions.explanation: The Beowulf poet places Grendel in the lineage of Cain, the first murderer in Genesis 4, establishing the monster's evil within a Biblical framework.

questions.question: What is the earliest surviving poem in the English language?
questions.explanation: Caedmon's Hymn (c. 670 AD) is the earliest surviving English poem — and it is a song of praise to God the Creator.

questions.question: In The Canterbury Tales, which character does Chaucer present as the ideal of a faithful Christian minister?
questions.explanation: Chaucer's Parson is poor in worldly goods but rich in holiness, teaching Christ's gospel truly and living it himself before preaching to others.

questions.question: What was John Milton's stated purpose in writing Paradise Lost?
options: To justify the ways of God to men
To criticize the Church of England
questions.explanation: Milton explicitly stated that his purpose was to 'justify the ways of God to men' — to show that God is just and good even in allowing the Fall of Man.

questions.question: Which Elizabethan concept held that the universe was organized in a divinely established hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The Great Chain of Being was the Elizabethan understanding that God had established a hierarchy extending from Himself through angels, humans, animals, plants, and minerals.

questions.question: Who wrote The Pilgrim's Progress while imprisoned for his faith?
questions.explanation: John Bunyan, a Puritan preacher, wrote The Pilgrim's Progress during his twelve years of imprisonment for unlicensed preaching.

questions.question: Which Victorian novelist used A Christmas Carol to present an essentially Christian conversion narrative?
questions.explanation: Dickens's A Christmas Carol shows Scrooge transformed from selfishness to generosity through encounters that mirror divine judgment and grace.

questions.question: What term did J.R.R. Tolkien coin for the sudden joyous turn in a story when unexpected deliverance comes?
questions.explanation: Tolkien coined 'eucatastrophe' to describe the sudden, joyous turn from seeming disaster to unexpected salvation — which he saw as a reflection of the Resurrection.

questions.question: Which modernist poet converted to Christianity in 1927 and went on to write deeply devotional poetry?
questions.explanation: T.S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, converted to Anglican Christianity in 1927 and produced devotional masterpieces including Ash Wednesday and Four Quartets.

questions.question: In Mere Christianity, what argument does C.S. Lewis use to point to God's existence?
options: The argument from design in nature
The moral argument — the universal sense of right and wrong points to a moral Lawgiver
The cosmological argument from first cause
questions.explanation: Lewis argues that the universal moral law — the sense of right and wrong that all humans recognize — points to a moral Lawgiver beyond humanity: God.
